<objective>
Implement R3 from the UI design review (260924-nho) as a **report-only** tool. The report makes hand-copy drift visible without touching any plugin. It covers two things:

1. **Component canon drift.** For every plugin, it reports whether the tooltip renderer (`setupTooltips` family), hover-help init (`initializeTipsToggle` family), knob binding (`bindKnob`) and knob visual (`updateKnobVisual`) match the O-ReverseDelay canon. The canon is held as data in the new `scripts/ui-canon.js`, modelled on `scripts/i18n-canon.js`.
2. **Module-copy forks.** Every tracked copy under `plugins/` of a `modules/` file (preset-manager.js ×12, tuning-panel.js ×4, tuning-panel.css ×3 at HEAD) is reported as MATCH or FORK by content hash.

The report is wired into the `ui-static-gates` CI job as a non-failing step.

Purpose: R3 turns the 13–22 hand-copied variants per component into a burn-down list. The review measured it: hand-copy **with** a canon gate gave 1 variant across 44 copies (i18n); hand-copy **without** a gate gave 13–22. The tool is report-only because converging a plugin onto canon is a behaviour change. Per R3 that is done one plugin at a time via `/improve` with a version bump, never as a sweep. This plan therefore edits nothing under `plugins/`.

Output: `scripts/ui-canon.js` (new), `scripts/check-ui-canon.js` (new), and one added step plus a header-comment line in `.github/workflows/ui-static-gates.yml`.

Design decisions this plan fixes (the planning context asked for them to be settled):
- **Canon source: embedded data, not the live file.** Canon is machine-copied from `git show <sha>:plugins/O-ReverseDelay/Source/ui/public/js/app.js`. `<sha>` is the last commit that touched that file, recorded in `UI_CANON_SOURCE` (at planning time `ed1fc465e679…`, O-ReverseDelay v1.20.0; the executor recomputes it). A canon read from the live file would move on every O-ReverseDelay `/improve` and silently redefine the target for 43 plugins. With embedded data, a re-anchor is a deliberate, reviewed diff of `scripts/ui-canon.js`. O-ReverseDelay is then measured like every other plugin.
- **Storage format: `//|`-prefixed line comments between sentinels, not i18n-canon's `/* … */` trick.** The canon functions contain `*/`: `bindKnob` has `/* already released */` and `initTipsToggle` has `/* private mode: … */`. Either would close an enclosing block comment. With a line prefix, backticks, `${…}` and `*/` are all inert, and no text is escaped.
- **Components are name groups, because O-ReverseDelay does not use the drifting names.** It defines no `setupTooltips` and no `initializeTipsToggle`. Its renderer is split across five functions and its switch across two. So each component has canon names (O-ReverseDelay's) and aliases (the names other plugins use). The report prints which names it found, so "setupTooltips diverges" is literally visible.
- **Three tiers of comparison.** `canon` means exact after stripping comments and whitespace. `shape` means identical code where only string-literal text differs. Example: a plugin that copies `initTipsToggle` verbatim but keeps its own localStorage key. Without this tier, such a plugin would read as a variant forever. `v:<hash>` means the code differs, and identical variants share a hash.
</objective>

  <action>
**Anchor the canon (R3; canon source = embedded data, per this plan's design decisions).**

1. Compute `SHA=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- plugins/O-ReverseDelay/Source/ui/public/js/app.js)`.
2. Read the plugin version from the quoted `VERSION` line of `git show ${SHA}:plugins/O-ReverseDelay/CMakeLists.txt`.

Use this one SHA for all three tasks. If another session commits O-ReverseDelay later, do not re-anchor.

**Create `scripts/ui-canon.js`.**

- Start with the same AGPL-3.0 header block as `scripts/i18n-canon.js`.
- Write a doc header in the same voice. It must explain:
  - why the canon is DATA and not a live read (the re-anchor argument in this plan's objective);
  - why storage uses `//|` line comments, not a block comment (the canon contains `*/`);
  - that this is REPORT-ONLY, and that converging a plugin is a per-plugin `/improve` with a version bump, never a sweep (R3);
  - the re-anchor procedure: run `node scripts/check-ui-canon.js --emit-canon <rev>`, replace the block from the BEGIN sentinel line through the END sentinel line with its stdout, then update `UI_CANON_SOURCE`.
- Export `UI_CANON_SOURCE`, an object with:
  - `plugin: 'O-ReverseDelay'`;
  - `file: 'plugins/O-ReverseDelay/Source/ui/public/js/app.js'`;
  - `commit`: the full 40-hex SHA;
  - `version`: for example '1.20.0'.
- Export `COMPONENTS`, an array of `{ id, label, canon: [names], aliases: [names] }`. In this task it holds ONLY `{ id: 'knob-visual', label: 'knob visual', canon: ['updateKnobVisual'], aliases: [] }`.
- Export `CANON_BEGIN` and `CANON_END`, the sentinel strings. Assemble each at runtime by concatenation (for example `'<<<UI_CANON_' + 'BEGIN>>>'`), so the file's own code cannot match them. This is the same trick i18n-canon.js uses. The doc header and every other comment in this file must also never spell a whole sentinel. The self-read locates the FIRST line that contains one, so a literal sentinel in the header would hijack the extraction.
- Export `readCanonText()`. It must:
  - read the file's own source (`fs.readFileSync(__filename)`);
  - locate the line holding `CANON_BEGIN` and the line holding `CANON_END`;
  - require every line strictly between them to start with `//|`, stripping a leading `//| ` or a bare `//|`;
  - join the stripped lines with newlines and return the result.
  - THROW with a specific message if either sentinel is missing, the sentinels are out of order, any in-block line lacks the prefix (report its line number), or the result is empty ("an empty canon makes every comparison vacuous").

  Extraction is lazy (a function, not done at load), so the file loads even while the block is empty. `--emit-canon` needs that.
- The block itself is two comment lines, `// ` + BEGIN sentinel and `// ` + END sentinel, with the `//|` lines between them. Generate it with `--emit-canon` (below) and splice it in with a small node one-liner. **Never hand-type canon text.**

**Create `scripts/check-ui-canon.js`.** Start with the AGPL header and a doc header covering:
- what is compared, and the categories;
- what is scanned;
- that the report always exits 0;
- known limits: regex-versus-division is a heuristic, and a desynced scan can only produce a false VARIANT, never a false canon, because canon is exact equality;
- that CI runs it with continue-on-error.

The script `require`s `./ui-canon.js`, `./serve-ui.js` and `./i18n-extract.js`, plus the node built-ins `fs`, `path`, `crypto` and `child_process`. No npm dependencies.

Build these parts, in this order:

(a) **`lexJs(src)`**
- Strip a leading BOM and convert CRLF to LF.
- Return tokens `{t, v, s, e}` where `t` is one of: ws, comment, word, punct, str, tq, regex.
  - **word**: a run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` or any code point ≥ 0x80.
  - **punct**: a single character.
  - **str**: `'…'` or `"…"`, honouring backslash escapes, and stopping at the closing quote or an unescaped newline.
  - **tq (template-quasi pieces)**: a piece runs from a backtick, or from the `}` that closes an interpolation, through the next `${` or closing backtick, inclusive. Keep a stack: push `'tmpl'` on `${` and `'brace'` on a punct `{`. On `}`, pop the stack; if the popped entry is `'tmpl'`, lex the next quasi piece starting at that `}`. This makes interpolations real code, with nesting.
  - **comment**: `//` to end of line, or `/*` to `*/`.
  - **regex**: a `/` that starts neither `//` nor `/*` is a regex when there is no previous significant token, or when the previous one is either:
    - a punct in `( , = : [ ! & | ? { } ; + - * % ~ ^ < >`, or
    - a word in {return, typeof, instanceof, in, of, new, delete, void, throw, case, do, else, yield, await}.

    Otherwise it is punct division. A regex body runs to an unescaped `/` outside a `[…]` class. If a newline comes first, emit the `/` as punct instead. Flags `[a-z]*` follow.
- Every loop iteration must advance at least one character.
- Unterminated constructs run to end of file. The lexer never throws on bad input.

(b) **`extractFunctions(src, tokens)`**
- Walk the significant tokens looking for: word `function`, an optional punct `*`, a word NAME, then punct `(`.
- Match parentheses to the closing `)`. The next significant token must be punct `{`. Match `{`/`}` using punct tokens only; tq, str, regex and comment tokens hide their braces.
- Start at the preceding `async` word if there is one. The text is `src.slice(start, closeBrace.e)`.
- Resume the scan just after NAME, not after the body, so nested declarations are found.
- An unmatched body is recorded as a parse warning, never thrown.
- Return `{name, text, tokens, start}`.

(c) **`normExact(tokens)` and `normShape(tokens)`**
- `normExact`: drop ws and comment tokens. Concatenate the texts, inserting one space only where the previous text ends AND the next begins with a word character.
- `normShape`: the same, but every str token becomes `"S"`, and every tq piece keeps its delimiters (a leading backtick or `}`, a trailing `${` or backtick) with its inner text replaced by `S`.
- `hash` is sha256 hex. `short` is its first 8 characters.

(d) **`pluginSources(name, repoRoot, moduleBasenames)`**
- `uiRoot` comes from `resolveUiRoot`. If null, the plugin row reads `(no UI root)`; that is not an error.
- Include the inline scripts of `uiRoot/index.html` via `scanHtml`: tag `script`, non-empty `raw`, and type '' | module | text/javascript. Label them `index.html <script #k>`.
- Include every `*.js`/`*.mjs` under `uiRoot`, found recursively, with these exclusions:
  - skip any path containing the segment `js/juce/`, or a `modules` or `node_modules` directory segment;
  - skip any basename in `moduleBasenames`, the set of `.js` basenames found by walking `repoRoot/modules`, so vendored copies are derived, never listed;
  - skip bundles: a basename matching `.bundle.js` or `.min.js`, any line over 2000 characters, or a file containing `sourceMappingURL=`.
- ALSO include `<plugin>/Source/ui/src/**/*.js` under the same exclusions when it exists. These are bundler sources; O-TextureForge's authored code lives there while its `public/js/app.bundle.js` is excluded.
- Sort by relative path for determinism.
- A plugin with a UI root but zero sources prints a `no JS sources found` note. It is never silently all-absent.

(e) **Classification (simple form for this task)**
- Collect defs of every canon and alias name across all sources.
- **canon**: each canon name defined exactly once, and the joined `normExact` of the canon-name defs, in canon order and joined with a newline, equals the canon's.
- **shape**: the same comparison on `normShape` is equal.
- **variant** `v:<short>`: any def exists but neither of the above holds. The hash is over all found defs: canon order, then alias order, then source order.
- **absent** `—`: no def exists.
- Canon side: run `readCanonText()` through the same lexer and extractor. Every canon name must be found exactly once. Otherwise print `CANON BROKEN: <component> <name> found N times`, mark that component's cells `CANON?`, and carry on.

(f) **Report**
- Header lines:
  - `check-ui-canon — REPORT-ONLY (exit 0 always)`;
  - `canon: O-ReverseDelay v<version> @ <short sha> <file>`;
  - a per-component canon hash line;
  - `plugins scanned: <N> (UI root resolved: <M>)`.
- A matrix: one row per plugin, the name padded to a fixed width, then one cell per component in COMPONENTS order. Cells read `canon` | `shape` | `v:xxxxxxxx` | `—` | `ERR`, separated by at least two spaces.
- Then a per-component block:
  - a counts line: `<id>: canon N · shape N · variant N (distinct N) · absent N · error N`;
  - one line per name in canon+aliases, formatted exactly as `    <name>: defined in <N> plugins`, where N is the number of plugins with at least one declaration;
  - group lines, largest first: `  canon ×N  <plugins>`, `  v:xxxxxxxx ×N  [<names found>]  <plugins>`, `  absent ×N  <plugins>`.

(g) **CLI**
- `--repo-root <dir>` (default `serve-ui.REPO_ROOT`).
- `--plugin <Name>`: filter to one plugin. An unknown name prints a message.
- `--emit-canon <rev>`:
  - Validate `rev` against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/~^-]{0,99}$` (no leading dash, so no option injection).
  - Run `execFileSync('git', ['show', rev + ':' + UI_CANON_SOURCE.file], {cwd: the real repo root, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 64 MB})`, with an argv array and no shell.
  - Extract every canon name of every component, in COMPONENTS order and deduplicated. Each must be defined exactly once, else print an error to stderr.
  - Print to stdout: the BEGIN comment line; each function's lines prefixed `//| ` (a bare `//|` for empty lines), with one bare `//|` line between functions; then the END comment line.
  - Print `git rev-parse` of the rev and that revision's CMake `VERSION` to stderr as a hint.
- `--self-test`: prints `SELF-TEST PASS n/n (skipped k)` or `SELF-TEST FAIL <ids>`. In this task it holds:
  - **L1**: an in-script fixture. Function `trap` has a body containing `'}'`, `"{"`, the nested template `` `a${ {b: 1}.b }c${ `x${'}'}` }` ``, `/[}{]/g`, `return /}/.test(s)`, a division `n / 12` both in code and inside an interpolation, and a `}` inside both a line comment and a block comment. It is followed by `function after() { return 1; }`.
    - Assert that `trap`'s extracted text ends exactly where a marker comment placed right after its closing brace begins.
    - Assert that `after` is extracted with body `{ return 1; }`.
    - NEGATIVE CONTROL: a naive brace counter, local to the self-test and blind to strings, comments and regex, run on the same fixture, must NOT end `trap` at the same offset. This proves the fixture really contains traps.
  - **L2**: `async function outer() { function inner() {} }`. Both names are found, and `outer`'s text starts at `async`.

**Exit discipline (report-only).**
- Wrap the whole main in try/catch. On an unexpected error, print `check-ui-canon: internal error — <msg>` and still exit 0.
- Wrap each plugin in its own try/catch, so one failure yields an `ERR` cell with the message listed at the end and the rest continue.
- Finish with an explicit exit code of 0 in every mode.

- In the header comment, add one line under the gate list naming `scripts/check-ui-canon.js` as a REPORT-ONLY step that never fails the job (R3).
- Change nothing else: the three existing steps, `permissions`, triggers and node version stay byte-identical.

    - **N1 (exact tier, a pair).**
      - The canon text reflowed (all whitespace runs doubled) with comments inserted is classified `canon`.
      - NEGATIVE: the canon text with the first `const ` token changed to `let ` is classified `variant`.
    - **N2 (shape tier, a pair).**
      - The canon text with one string literal's content changed (for example `"tips-toggle"` → `"help-toggle"` inside `initTipsToggle`) is classified `shape`, not `canon`.
      - The same text with a code token changed as well is classified `variant`.
    - **N3 (absent and non-decl).**
      - Source with no component names → `absent`.
      - Source whose only binding is `const bindKnob = (el) => {}` → `nd` (non-decl), not absent.
    - **G1 (grouping).**
      - Two identical mutated sources get the same short hash.
      - Two differently mutated sources get different hashes.
    - **M1 (multi-definition).**
      - A source that declares `updateKnobVisual` twice, with the canon body both times, is `variant`, never canon, and its found-name label shows `updateKnobVisual×2`.
    - **N4 (canon integrity).**
      - `readCanonText()` yields every canon name of every component exactly once.
      - When `git cat-file -e ${UI_CANON_SOURCE.commit}` succeeds, the `--emit-canon` output for that commit equals the block in `ui-canon.js`, with trailing whitespace per line ignored.

  </read_first>
  <action>
**Module-copy census (R3, second half: "tracked copies match `modules/` by content hash, forks flagged"; tuning-panel.css included, as the planning context allows).**

(a) **Module map.** Walk `repoRoot/modules`, skipping `node_modules`, for `*.js` and `*.css`, building `basename → [repo-relative module paths]`. This is derived, never a transcribed list; at HEAD it yields 7 files.

(b) **Tracked list.**
- If `git -C repoRoot rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds AND its `fs.realpathSync` equals `fs.realpathSync(repoRoot)`, use `git -C repoRoot ls-files -z -- plugins` via `execFileSync` with an argv array, and label the source `git ls-files`.
- Otherwise walk `repoRoot/plugins` (skipping `.git`, `node_modules` and `build`) and label the source `filesystem walk (not a git work tree)`. A `git archive` snapshot contains only tracked files, so the walk is exact there.
- Print the label in the header.

(c) **Copies.** A copy is a listed file under `plugins/` whose basename is in the module map. For each copy:
- `sha256` of its bytes, with CRLF converted to LF, compared with each module file of that basename, converted the same way. The result is `MATCH` if equal to any, else `FORK`. If the basename maps to more than one module file, set `ambiguous: true`.
- `lines`: the copy's line count and the module's line count.
- `ships`: `yes` when `path.resolve` of the copy equals the `abs` of any `binaryDataSources(plugin, repoRoot)` entry, else `no`.
- `sync`: `configure` when all three hold, else `frozen`:
  - the copy's plugin-relative path is exactly `Source/ui/public/modules/<basename>`;
  - the module file sits at `<moduleDir>/js/<basename>`;
  - the plugin's `readCmake` text has an `ouaricon_add_module(<target> <moduleDirName> …)` call, taking the first two whitespace-separated arguments.

  A frozen MATCH is still worth seeing, because it becomes a fork on the next module bump.

(d) **Direct embeds.** Per plugin, list the `binaryDataSources` entries whose `abs` lies under `repoRoot/modules/`, as repo-relative paths. Title the section `direct embeds (build reads modules/ itself — zero drift by construction)`.

**Report sections, appended after the component blocks.**

- `── tracked module copies vs modules/ (sha256, CRLF-normalised; tracked list: <label>)`: one row per copy, showing plugin, plugin-relative path, status, `lines copy/module`, `ships`, `sync`. Sort FORK before MATCH, then by plugin.
- `── direct embeds …`: one line per plugin.
- `── summary`:
  - one line per component, restating its counts line;
  - one line per module basename, formatted exactly as `  <basename>: <copies> tracked copies — <m> MATCH, <f> FORK`;
  - a total line;
  - the closing line `REPORT-ONLY — exit 0`.
- When `--plugin` is given, all sections are filtered to that plugin.

**`--json` mode.** Print ONE JSON document and no human text. Keys:
- `tool: 'check-ui-canon'`, `reportOnly: true`;
- `canon`: UI_CANON_SOURCE plus the per-component canon hashes;
- `repoRoot`, `trackedListSource`;
- `plugins`: `[{ name, uiRoot, sources: [labels], components: { <id>: { status, hash, shapeHash, found, alsoFound, nonDecl } }, notes, error }]`;
- `components`: `{ <id>: { counts, definedBy: { <name>: [plugins] }, groups: [{ status, hash, names, plugins }] } }`;
- `trackedCopies`: `[{ plugin, path, module, status, ambiguous, lines, moduleLines, ships, sync }]`;
- `directEmbeds`: `[{ plugin, files }]`;
- `errors`: `[{ scope, message }]`.

**Resilience (report-only means it never fails, and never hides that it failed).**
- Each section and each plugin is individually try/caught. Errors are printed in an `── errors` section, or in the `errors` array under `--json`.
- If zero plugins were scanned, print `WARNING: 0 plugins scanned — the scanner found nothing, which is not a clean result`. A run that found nothing has stopped looking.
- `--repo-root` pointing at a missing path prints an error line.
- Every one of these still exits 0.

**Header.** Update the doc header of `scripts/check-ui-canon.js` to cover:
- the census;
- the `sync` meaning;
- that direct embeds are listed but never compared, since they have no drift by construction;
- that untracked configure-time copies are out of scope. They are gitignored, and the build refreshes them.

**Commit.**

2. `git commit -m "feat(quick-260924-s7n): R3 check-ui-canon — tracked module-copy fork census, direct embeds, --json, exit-0 resilience" -- scripts/check-ui-canon.js`.

  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| repo content → report tool | Plugin JS, HTML and CMake are parsed by a hand-written lexer. Malformed or pathological input must not hang or crash the job, and must not produce a false "canon" |
| CLI args → git subprocess | The `--emit-canon <rev>` and `--repo-root` values reach `git` and the filesystem |
| CI runner → repository | The new step runs on every push to main, inside a job with `contents: read` |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-s7n-01 | Tampering (argument injection) | check-ui-canon.js subprocesses (`--emit-canon` show, ls-files, rev-parse) | medium | mitigate | `execFileSync` with an argv array and no shell. `rev` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/~^-]{0,99}$`, so no leading dash and no option injection. Verified in Task 3 by an invalid-rev run that exits 0 and executes nothing |
| T-s7n-02 | Denial of Service | lexJs / extractFunctions on unterminated or pathological input | low | mitigate | Every lexer iteration advances at least one character, and unterminated constructs run to EOF. Per-plugin try/catch. CI step `timeout-minutes: 2` inside the job's existing 5-minute cap |
| T-s7n-03 | Repudiation / integrity of the report | Classification after a lexer desync | low | mitigate | Canon is exact equality, so a desynced scan can only yield a false VARIANT, never a false canon. Paired positive and negative self-test controls (L1 has a naive-counter negative control; N1, N2 and G1 are pairs) prove the lexer and classifier are not inert |
| T-s7n-04 | Elevation of Privilege | ui-static-gates.yml | low | mitigate | `permissions: contents: read` unchanged. No secrets and no `npm install`, since the tool uses Node built-ins only. The three existing gate steps are asserted byte-identical in Task 1's verify |
| T-s7n-05 | Tampering (collateral edits) | plugins/ (other sessions' uncommitted O-Formant work, PLUGINS.md) | medium | mitigate | The tool only reads, and `--emit-canon` writes to stdout only. Commits are path-scoped with explicit `git add` of the two new files, and branch/status are re-checked before each commit. Task 3 proves the union of the three commits' file lists is exactly the three planned files. Corpus runs use a temp `git archive` snapshot, never `git stash` or checkout |
| T-s7n-06 | Information Disclosure | Report output in CI logs | low | accept | The output is repo-relative paths and content hashes of a public repository (public origin since 2026-08-03). Nothing secret is read |
| T-s7n-SC | Tampering (supply chain) | package installs | low | accept | No npm, pip or cargo installs in this plan. The tool uses Node built-ins and in-repo modules only |
</threat_model>
